report:
## What the evidence actually shows

Your sister's belief likely stems from early, small, and low-quality studies (some later found to include data irregularities or fraud) that suggested large mortality reductions with ivermectin. Those early "meta-analyses" pooled weak evidence and produced dramatic-looking results (e.g., risk ratios around 0.38), but subsequent, larger, well-designed trials have not confirmed this.

The most rigorous test is the **TOGETHER trial** (NEJM, 2022), a large randomized, placebo-controlled trial in Brazil. It found **no significant reduction in hospitalization, disease progression, or death** with ivermectin compared to placebo (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2115869). A follow-up higher-dose ivermectin trial (JAMA, 2023) also found **no mortality or hospitalization benefit** even at a higher, longer-duration dose (https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2801827).

The **Cochrane systematic review**, which aggregates and quality-weights all major RCTs, concluded that ivermectin **has no beneficial effect** on mortality or other clinical outcomes in COVID-19 patients (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8248252/, superseded by later Cochrane updates reaching the same conclusion).

Consistent with this evidence, the **World Health Organization** now explicitly recommends **against** using ivermectin for COVID-19 outside of clinical trials, citing lack of convincing benefit and no strong biological plausibility (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivermectin_during_the_COVID-19_pandemic; https://www.who.int/news-room/feature-stories/detail/who-advises-that-ivermectin-only-be-used-to-treat-covid-19-within-clinical-trials).

**Bottom line:** The claim that ivermectin lowers COVID-19 mortality is **not supported by the highest-quality current evidence**. Early promising results came from smaller, lower-quality, or flawed studies. Large randomized trials and systematic reviews (Cochrane, WHO) consistently find no significant mortality benefit, and major health authorities recommend against its use for COVID-19 treatment.
